fields.subnational_unit: rural Bangladesh; 275 villages (Bangladesh Integrated Household Survey, round 3, 2018-2019)
fields.population: adult primary woman and man respondents (typically household head and spouse) in rural households who could participate in local water management organisations (WMOs)
fields.sample_size: 11,209 adult respondents in the survey sample (5,604 households; 275 villages); 10,173 in the mediation model; analytical sample 5,512 women and 4,532 men
fields.effect_measure: multiple mediation analysis (seemingly unrelated regressions with village-clustered standard errors) of the gender gap in WMO participation (attended at least one of the last five meetings) through decision-making autonomy, access to agricultural information, efficacy and hours of work
fields.effect_estimate: Participation is very low and lower for women: 0.77% of women and 2.03% of men in the full sample (chi-square 30.085, p < 0.001); 1.75% and 4.62% where a WMO exists (chi-square 31.105, p < 0.001). Total gender effect on the probability of participation about -0.012. Women's lower household decision-making autonomy mediates 9% of the gap (p < 0.001) and lower access to agricultural information 14% (p = 0.040); jointly 22% (p = 0.004). Efficacy and hours of work do not mediate (not significant). Rare outcome; estimates may be sensitive to the sample.
fields.adjusted_or_unadjusted: adjusted (individual, household and village controls; division dummies)
fields.covariates: age, at least one year of formal education, agricultural land owned (standardised), household and village-level controls, division dummies; household headship discussed as a possible omitted mediator
fields.model_type: multiple mediation via seemingly unrelated regressions (linear probability) with village-clustered confidence intervals; logistic regressions by gender in the appendix
fields.study_design: cross-sectional analysis of a nationally representative household survey
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: Low concern (appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text; supersedes the sparse-extraction 'High concern' of 2026-09-28; JBI Cross Sectional items 1-8: Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes; 8/8 Yes). Basis: sample frame and eligibility described (BIHS primary man and woman respondents); setting and 275 villages described; gender measured directly; participation defined as attendance at recent meetings, distinguished from nominal membership; individual, household and village confounders and division dummies included; mediation models with village clustering. Caveats: self-reported attendance, an extremely rare outcome (the authors warn of sensitivity), observational data with possible endogeneity (headship) and no causal claim.
fields.section: Full text (Ecology and Society 31(2):17): Abstract; Data and methods; Results; Discussion; Appendix 1
fields.exact_location: Abstract p1; data and methods p5-8 (sample, dependent variable, mediators, controls); results p8-12 (Tables 1-3); appendix 1

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a cross-sectional analysis of the nationally representative Bangladesh Integrated Household Survey (n = 10,173 in the mediation model) of why women participate less in local water management organisations, read in full text 2026-10-04. Women 0.77% vs men 2.03% attended recent meetings; decision-making autonomy and information access mediate 22% of the gap. Self-reported, rare outcome, observational; the exposure is gender, not a legal or administrative rule.
